Top 10 best EFL League One stadiums for atmosphere so far this season

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Football is a game that can be decided by the finest of margins, with the quality of a team's players, the coach's tactical approach, and individual moments of brilliance often determining the outcome of a match. However, there is another factor that can be just as influential on any given afternoon — the supporters in the stands.

Sources indicate that A passionate home crowd can undoubtedly act as a 12th man, lifting players when their energy levels begin to drop, inspiring late winners, and making life incredibly uncomfortable for visiting teams. League One has never been short of grounds capable of producing a raucous atmosphere, and the 2026/27 campaign has provided another reminder of just how special the third tier can be.

Attendances are set to be particularly impressive this season, with Leicester City and Sheffield Wednesday bringing sizeable fanbases into the division following relegation, while the likes of Bradford City, Huddersfield Town, Reading, Barnsley, and Milton Keynes Dons also have stadiums capable of hosting substantial crowds.

These established EFL outfits continue to attract impressive support, but there is also plenty of intrigue elsewhere, with clubs boasting their own traditions, expectations, and rivalries all competing for promotion. The sheer variety of grounds and fanbases makes for a compelling campaign both on and off the pitch, with some seriously impressive attendances expected throughout the season.

But which grounds have generated the best atmosphere so far this season? From intimidating, old-school football stadiums to the more modern arenas that come alive on massive occasions, these are 10 League One venues that deserve recognition for the noise, passion and energy coming from their supporters.

Sources indicate that the Select Car Leasing Stadium is hosting a joyful and defiant party right now, proving that raw spreadsheets completely lie when assessing football passion. On paper, a stadium running at roughly 47% capacity should feel dead. In reality, after years of exhausting ownership turmoil and points deductions, this young and exciting Reading team has the fans emotionally reinvested. The core home sections have consolidated, turning their matchdays into a loud celebration of survival. They might not fill the entire ground, but the fans who do show up make a serious racket, showing you can prioritise passionate vocal energy over empty seating stats.

On a spreadsheet, Meadow Lane's sub-65% fullness percentage looks like an atmosphere killer, but on the terraces, the traditional core of this club tells an entirely different story. This is a historic stadium backed by a deeply loyal and multi-generational fanbase that understands the assignment on matchdays. They don't rely on plastic clappers or manufactured noise; the support for Notts County is entirely organic. When the matchday script delivers a big moment, the old stands respond with a booming roar that carries real emotional weight. It is a pure and old-school football environment that relies heavily on a passionate foundation.

In a recent development, there is no denying that the general mood around Hillsborough is significantly healthier than it has been in past periods of turbulence, even if the sleeping giant still requires a bit of an extra spark on the pitch. Averaging a massive 31,000-plus crowd in the third tier means that when Sheffield Wednesday truly click, the ceiling for raw volume is unparalleled. The concern is the sheer size of the stadium bowl. If the team isn't delivering a high-intensity performance, the sound can easily get lost in the vacant pockets of a 39,000-capacity ground. It requires a specific catalyst to get the entire stadium rocking but should be a 12th man this season if Dave Challinor can get things going.

Architecturally, the Kassam Stadium shouldn't work for atmosphere, yet the local faithful have turned this structural handicap into a point of defiance by roaring loud and proud from three sides of the ground. Lacking a stand behind one goal can easily cause sound to escape and drain the intensity right out of a matchday. Yet, by packing out the remaining three stands and averaging nearly 80% fullness, the Oxford United crowd stays remarkably tight-knit. The noise bounces sharply between the side stands, generating a surprisingly intense and concentrated din. It is a scrappy environment that proves fan engagement can easily overcome quirky stadium blueprints.

Industry observers note that sitting at the summit of League One has completely revitalised the mood around the club, placing the home atmosphere on a clear upward curve. While the stadium’s raw fullness percentage presently sits lower at 68.7%, the underlying metrics show an atmosphere on a sharp upward trajectory. Winning football has restored a sense of pride and confidence, meaning the core vocal sections for Huddersfield Town are noisier and more engaged than they have been in years. The ground acoustics handle the chants brilliantly when the crowd gets going. As these sustained performances and the brilliance of Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes inevitably coax more of the supporters back through the turnstiles, this venue will only march higher up the rankings between now and the end of the campaign.

In a recent development, physically, Kenilworth Road remains a uniquely temperamental cauldron and one of the most hostile and intimidating grounds in English football. The low tin roofs and tight, cramped architecture trap noise beautifully, turning the stadium into an absolute pressure cooker when the fans are up. However, high expectations following their recent journey have created a slightly tense backdrop this season. Because Luton Town haven't quite blown the division away until recent weeks, the home crowd has occasionally drifted into anxious silence. It remains a terrifying place for away teams to visit, but the vocal output is currently waiting for the team to consistently spark it and make it a 12th man.

Sources indicate that geographic isolation plays a massive role in the unique psychology of the Home Park atmosphere, turning the ground into a fortress for the Green Army. The fans treat every single home game like a major regional event, turning out in immense numbers and filling nearly 87% of the stadium's 18,173 capacity. That level of fan density in a closed-bowl setup creates a ferocious and echoing wall of sound. Because visiting away ends are rarely at full capacity due to the brutal travel distances, Plymouth Argyle supporters completely dominate the stadium’s acoustics, creating a heavily partisan cauldron that gives their team a massive statistical edge on home turf.

Which team has the best atmosphere in League One? The most intimidating? Comment your thoughts below!

In an era dominated by modern and often sterile bowls that systematically stifle organic support, the Abbey Stadium remains a glorious yet old-school sanctuary that offers the purest football culture in the league. Holding onto its traditional standing terraces keeps a gritty and authentic style thriving. Over 3,700 safe-standing spaces allow Cambridge United fans to gather, bounce, and generate noise organically rather than waiting for a cue on the pitch. The acoustic output punches completely above its weight relative to the ground's 8,127 capacity. It is aggressive, tightly packed, and serves as a brilliant reminder of why terrace culture is so vital to the soul of the EFL.

Recent findings suggest that there is a beautiful synchronicity between what is happening on the pitch and the racket being made off it at Edgeley Park right now, making them the division's undisputed kings of momentum. Backed by heavy investment and a clear upward trajectory, the Stockport County fanbase is completely unified, and that optimism translates into a relentless engine on matchday. The iconic Cheadle End serves as the focal point, driving a constant wave of noise that rarely dips into flat lulls. It is an intensely vibrant and energetic environment where the players feed directly off the terrace energy. For a consistent, high-vibe atmosphere from the first whistle to the last, they are arguably the division's benchmark since their return to the third tier.

In a recent development, when it clicks at Valley Parade, it isn't just loud, it's completely suffocating for opposition players. Averaging over 19,000 fans in the third tier is a joke in itself, but it’s the structural layout that truly weaponises that data. The towering Kop end behaves like an acoustic amplifier. When the Bradford City home crowd is unified and driving forward, the sheer wall of sound generated behind that goal completely dwarfs everything else in League One. It alters how visiting teams defend, forcing rushed clearances and causing real panic. For raw and unadulterated volume that can visually unnerve an opponent, the Bantams easily take the crown on this list.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan were introduced to a newly introduced name this week: Brett Yormark. But who is he and what does he bring to the table?

With Milan’s announcement of a new company – Milan Sport and Entertainment – a new CEO was appointed to oversee things and develop the Milanese sporting project for RedBird and that CEO is Yormark.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For those who are unfamiliar with the new hire, he is obviously someone that Gerry Cardinale trusts heavily and this was stated in the American’s announcement of the MSE tech giant.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a fresh chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”.

However, what has his career looked like so far and how can he help the Rossoneri take the next level?

Recent findings suggest that in terms of his own reputation, he started his career working in selling TV time before moving to be a senior accountant at Palace Sports and Entertainment, sound familiar? From there, he got his first major move, becoming a director of marketing at NASCAR, where he stayed from 1998 to 2005.

After his early experience in basketball, he then moved away from the track and back onto the court where he joined the Brooklyn Jets as their new CEO. Tasked with transforming the club into a more modern brand, he franchised the club – taking them from Brooklyn to New Jersey – and brought several sports and events to the Barclays Center, which opened in 2012, as Sportico reported.

From there, he then headed to Roc Nation, taking a role as their ‘President & Chief of Branding and Strategy’. From artists to athletes, Yormark worked with some of the biggest names and brands in the world from 2019 to 2022 and was a major part of the brand earning the rights for the Super Bowl halftime indicates.

It’s worth noting that he’s also worked with Milan in this period, as they partnered in 2020. On a side note, it’ll be interesting to see if these links help any further with the ongoing speculation about the Diavolo and Endrick, who is also represented by the brand.

To join the Milan Sports and Entertainment firm, he leaves behind a role with Substantial 12, where he had held a role since the summer of 2022. Within his first few months as its commissioner, he secured media rights deals with ESPN and Fox to help stabilise the league.

The Kansas City Star continues, stating that he also oversaw expansions into ‘Arizona, Arizona State, Colorado and Utah’, as well as keeping men’s and women’s basketball in Kansas City.

It has been revealed that given that he’ll be working heavily with the hope of making a Milan NBA team, this is relevant experience. Importantly, too, he has already fought for sport in Kansas City, so doing the same for football (and basketball) in Milan will not be unfamiliar territory.

Furthermore, alongside Cardinale, he has experience in getting the most out of TV deals, so this should help the entertainment side of the tech giant take off as well.

Although he’s not got a background in football, the quality of his CV is undeniable and he’s thrived alongside the companies where he’s worked for years.

Recent findings suggest that he’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as major as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that swansea City saw head coach Vitor Matos’ departure confirmed on Wednesday. The Portuguese boss has left to take charge of RC Strasbourg, with the Swans receiving a compensation fee of around £5m and placing Leon Britton, Kris O’Leary and potentially Ashley Williams in charge on an interim basis.

The hunt for Matos’ replacement is on, and talkSPORT reporter Alex Crook states Welsh boss Rob Edwards and Liverpool first-team coach Tommy Elphick are contenders. The fresh news comes after reputable fanzine the Swansea Independent stated early talks with Edwards were held, and Elphick would be ‘open to discussions’.

Sources indicate that edwards is out of work and would not require compensation. Elphick’s role in Andoni Iraola’s backroom staff at Anfield means the Swans would have to pay a fee to bring him to South Wales if they wish.

Edwards and Elphick are two intriguing candidates in Swansea City’s search for a boss.

Of the two, Edwards is the most obvious. The Welshman is experienced at Championship level from his spells with Watford, Luton Town and Middlesbrough, and he has promotion pedigree to his name from his time with the Hatters. He had Boro flying too, before an ultimately ill-fated move to Wolves.

Like Matos, he favours high-intensity football, and his use of wide players at Luton Town could see him use the Swans’ squad effectively.

At the other end of the spectrum, Elphick has no senior management experience. He has emerged as a highly regarded coach since retiring in 2021, starting out in the Bournemouth youth setup before stepping into the senior side with Gary O’Neill and retaining his role after Andoni Iraola’s arrival.

Iraola took him to Liverpool with him in the summer. The fact he has never been the lead man in the dugout means we can’t know what to expect from his tactical blueprint, but if his principles are aligned with Iraola’s, expect fast ball progression and aggressive pressing.

Swansea City will be frustrated to lose another manager, just as they started to really build to something special. The same thing happened when Russell Martin was poached by Southampton.

Industry observers note that the Swans made great strides under Matos’ lead, so ideally they need a head coach who will oversee a similar tactical plan. It will help them work well with the existing squad and should limit teething problems after an unforeseen change in the dugout.

Swansea City will be carefully weighing up a number of candidates but there will be an eagerness to replace Matos as soon and efficiently as possible to limit how much it disrupts their season.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has remarked: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many challenges to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

Recent findings suggest that 'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response.

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'.

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'.

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

'The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every one of the expressions of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of its heart, maximum respect for his privacy, in these terrible moments.'.

Bradford City are potentially up for sale, with prospective Thai buyers linked to the League One club at present.

There is excitement building as takeover talk heats up at Bradford City before the midpoint of the 2026/27 League One season, with the January transfer window just over a month away.

Bradford are in an excellent position in the League One table to kick on, with Michael Duff taking over from Graham Alexander. However, they have fallen out of the automatic promotion places and fresh investment could kick them on, be that this season or next year.

FLW's Bradford City fan pundit Boris Thomson was asked about the fact Bradford are a surprise target for a Thai-based group who are thinking of a takeover bid.

The Bantams are flying high in League One and come backed by a big support and that has caught the eye of a group of Far East speculators who have had previous interest in buying EFL clubs.

Bradford could be for sale at the right price and the Thais are keen, so we asked what he makes of this news and if he would welcome a takeover. He said: "Seeing this news about a proposed Thai takeover and it's an interesting one.

"I'm not too clued-up at all on what the sort of financial regulations are for League One clubs. I assume that the brackets for financial fair play are of lower figures than in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that "We've all seen Man City. The first thing I will say is that I hope we are being incredibly careful with what we are doing, but it depends how incredibly large the financial backing is from the Thais.

"But I wouldn't not welcome it if that makes sense? But I'm not sure we need a revolution, at the moment. A bit more financial backing for Duff and particularly for David Sharpe would be a wonderful thing.

"They both know the club well enough now, maybe not Duff as much but Sharpe definitely, and he knows the club well enough to make the right investments for us in order to improve us on the pitch.

"I think a little more dosh available to help us with some real infrastructural problems would help. Like a training ground; that's the first one we need — to own a training ground.

According to recent reports, "I'm not going to jump on the bandwagon just yet. I probably need to hear more about it first, but then we'll see. I think a proposed takeover from a Thai consortium leaves a lot to be desired if the details aren't fully out there yet.".

One of the issues, as Boris states, is the training ground. However, it goes beyond that, with the stadium another aspect to consider in a £10 million issue for Bradford or investors going forwards.

Per The Yorkshire Post, Bradford have been giving some consideration to potentially leaving Valley Parade due to the cost of the rent for at least a decade-and-a-half now.

Earlier this year, the Bantams Supporters Trust entered into a period of consultation over what to do about the stadium with Bradford fans, with a valuation of it put at between £8 million and £10 million.

But when The Athletic's Matt Slater reported on the possibility of the Bantams being sold earlier this year back in March 2026, a potential sale price could be just £10 million as well, which could help if investment is needed into a training ground or new stadium entirely.

The recent valuation back in March seems very low for an upwardly mobile League One club, but there's a very good reason for this modest valuation, and it comes down to what the club doesn't own via the stadium.

That noted, Bradford fans should be excited, even if Boris is somewhat skeptical, as they have plenty of reasons to feel optimistic following recent reports linking the Thai-based consortium with a potential bid for the Bantams.

Fresh investment could provide newly introduced manager Michael Duff with the financial firepower needed to reignite their League One promotion push and finally return the West Yorkshire outfit to the Championship after a very long time away.

Will Bradford make it back to the Championship within two seasons? Comment below!

Crucially, current owner Stefan Rupp has previously insisted to The Telegraph and Argus that he would only pass the keys to ambitious buyers capable of taking the club forward, meaning any successful deal should guarantee serious backing.

Industry observers note that coupled with Bradford's massive 'one-club city' fanbase and potential Valley Parade stadium developments, a takeover could truly unlock this sleeping giant's long-awaited potential. They could be promoted without it, of course, but consolidating at a higher level would be easier with proper investment.

Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

Recent findings suggest that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

The hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

Matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

In a recent development, slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Recent findings suggest that gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is rolled out forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

It has been revealed that slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A new-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

Sebastien Pocognoli's first Scotland XI to take on Slovenia 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿Watch the game live on BBC One Scotland from 13:45 BST 📺#BBCFootball pic.twitter.com/OnfWR7Gp8C.

Debutants Robbie Ure and Stephen Welsh are each poised for their first international cap. Billy Gilmour returns to the starting XI after missing the World Cup through injury and Oli McBurnie will make his first appearance for Scotland since 2021.

Sébastien Pocognoli's first Scotland starting XI 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/JC6RGOq1QJ.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

“A good result can help but the most crucial thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

It has been revealed that “I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

“We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his newly introduced role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

AC Milan are desperate to add more quality and depth to their defence and two names are dominating the talk presently.

Ahead of the January mercato, there has been plenty of talk about Milan’s top target. It may well be Endrick or Nicolo Tresoldi, but the Rossoneri are also waiting to add a defender to Ruben Amorim’s squad and one name takes the headlines.

In this morning’s edition of Gazzetta dello Sport, as seen below, the headline is that the Rossoneri will make an assault for Inacio in January. Amorim is desperate to reunite with Sporting’s captain and the road there is certainly plausible to travel.

Industry observers note that if Goncalo Ramos was the man for the attack, his namesake will be the one to help the defence. So, whilst news of attackers dominates the headlines, at Casa Milan, it’s not all they’re thinking about.

Recent findings suggest that A deal for Inacio has been ‘pending since the summer’, and with the injury problems in the first half of the season, another defensive addition is a must. There is respect for the club from Inacio and whilst a deal still needs to be completed, their chances look good.

The order from Gerry Cardinale is clear: sign Inacio in January.

In the summer, there will be another reinforcement, hopefully. The idea of signing Virgil van Dijk has been touted heavily in recent days and Cardinale is determined to sign him for next season. So, on January 1, they can begin to start working on a pre-contract arrangement.

The Dutchman is ‘looking for a new challenge’ and a move to San Siro would provide that. A move similar to Zlatan Ibrahimovic’s return or even Luka Modric’s arrival, he’d bring a heap of experience at the top level, which is a must.

Inacio is the target for now, but then the attention will turn to van Dijk in defence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's not been the loan spell at Bradford City that QPR expected Kieran Morgan to have so far this season, with the 20-year-old struggling to get regular League One minutes under both Graham Alexander and Michael Duff.

Morgan was thrust into first-team action at Loftus Road as a teenager after arriving from Tottenham Hotspur in the summer of 2024.

He made 59 league appearances over two years, but after signing Glen Kamara to partner Nicolas Madsen and Jonathan Varane in the engine room this past summer, and with Ronnie Edwards able to anchor the midfield, the club sent Morgan out on loan to aid his development.

Sources indicate that joining Bradford seemed a great opportunity, with the Bantams coming off a third-place finish in their first season back at third-tier level in six years last season. It was the top-end League One move that could help bridge the gap towards regular Championship football upon his return.

Morgan has hardly had a look-in, though, and all signs point to the 20-year-old being sent elsewhere once the January transfer window opens.

Industry observers note that morgan arrived at Bradford late in the window, a few days out from Deadline Day. It's always difficult for young players to dislodge a settled partnership in the middle, especially after not being with the club for pre-season, and the QPR loanee has struggled to do so.

Recent findings suggest that the majority of his minutes have come in the Jersey Mike's Trophy, with starts in the FA Cup and EFL Cup, too. In League One, he's played just 41 minutes, being unused from the bench five times. Granted, he has come off the bench more under Michael Duff, who has used him in the last two.

Nevertheless, QPR will definitely have wanted more from Morgan from this loan spell, and FLW's Hoops fan pundit, Louis Moir, "wouldn't be surprised" if the 20-year-old was recalled.

"I wouldn't be surprised to see the club recall Morgan, purely just to send him somewhere where he's guaranteed to play," he said.

"He's got the ability to play consistently in League One, for sure. I think he got more experience than he could have imagined for us in the Championship and probably deserves to be playing a lot in League One.".

Moir did concede that it would have been difficult for Morgan to get into a Bradford side who, despite now sitting outside the top six, have been well-drilled and difficult to beat. A lot of that comes down to Antoni Sarcevic and Callum Connolly in the middle.

"He's joined Bradford, who are doing fairly well, so it's probably been difficult for him to go there and automatically play every week, so he's probably getting frustrated," he continued.

"For his own development, he'll likely be recalled and go to a club that agrees to play him most weeks.".

According to recent reports, moir went on to admit that Morgan's career at QPR has, so far, been quite peculiar. It's not often that an 18-year-old gets thrown into the action at Championship level and then, two years later, is sent out on loan to League One.

Ultimately, the midfielder can't control the number of injuries the Hoops have had, especially last season, which have given him minutes, but the fan pundit feels that his standing in Julien Stephan's side could be much better if his loan spell came before his time in the first-team fold at his parent club.

According to recent reports, "I wouldn't say he's too good to be warming the bench in League One. He's a decent player, but I think he was overhyped a little bit with us when he came and played in our first team," Moir admitted.

It has been revealed that "It revealed in his last few appearances for us. He was a bit lightweight and gave the ball away a lot, I noticed. He was probably rushed into the team with us and should have gone on loan a lot sooner.

Sources indicate that "His career has almost gone the opposite way. He should have been on loan last year and then may have been good enough for us now, but yeah, if he doesn't improve at Bradford, bring him back and send him out somewhere where he'll play and go with that until the summer.".

Industry observers note that morgan hasn't played for QPR yet this season, luckily enough, so the Hoops will be able to send him to play elsewhere if they so wish. Moir hopes he gets the game time he needs, as he feels his chances of playing regularly at Loftus Road again are slipping away.

"I'll be surprised if he makes it properly at QPR, making the first team week in, week out," he concluded.

It may be a bit dramatic to say, given Morgan is only 20 years old, but with QPR improving rapidly over the last three months or so without the ex-Spurs academy man in the team, worries are seeping in that they may have outgrown him.

In a recent development, morgan was a useful squad option at Loftus Road both in the 2024/25 campaign and in Julien Stephan's first season in charge last year. Being sent out on loan this year would have been a massive opportunity for the 20-year-old to prove that he's more than just a sporadic option.

Recent findings suggest that who do you think could loan Kieran Morgan and give him game time, if he's recalled from Bradford City? Let us know in the comments.

It hasn't worked out at all, though, and if Morgan can't get into the Bradford side regularly, the chances of him coming back and dislodging Madsen or Kamara, if the Finnish international stays past his loan spell, are very slim.

It has been revealed that the 20-year-old needs game time not only for his own development, but for a chance to prove himself to his parent club, too. If he's going to get back into the QPR picture, a big January decision will need to be made.

Significant Leicester City ownership revision emerges after being listed for £200m in August

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City have had financial problems for some time now, and discontent towards long-term owners King Power has grown amid the club’s 10-year slide from Premier League champions to League One.
  • Now though, after limited progress and minimal news, The Telegraph has reported that the Foxes are no longer up for sale.
  • Despite their debt, the club were valued at £200m upon being listed for sale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City have had financial problems for some time now, and discontent towards long-term owners King Power has grown amid the club’s 10-year slide from Premier League champions to League One. As a result of growing unrest and dire finances, LCFC were put up for sale in August.

Now though, after limited progress and minimal news, The Telegraph has reported that the Foxes are no longer up for sale. Senior staff in Leicestershire have been informed by the Thai leadership that the club is off the market with the full focus on winning League One promotion.

Despite their debt, the club were valued at £200m upon being listed for sale. This valuation and the owners’ refusal to lower their asking price has proven a major stumbling block, and now there will be no takeover at the King Power Stadium.

Chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha was reluctant to list Leicester City for sale in the first place. He and the King Power ownership have consistently expressed a desire to lead the club back from their poor position and to their previous heights.

However, being put up for sale and entertaining takeover bids indicated that the ownership had realised they had done all they could to try and salvage the club to no avail. But, with a £200m valuation and tremendous debts, LCFC have proven a hard sell – despite their modern training ground and stature.

It means the supporters will have to stick it out with the current hierarchy for some time yet. The chairman and his close affiliate Jon Rudkin have been heavily scrutinised in recent years, but despite a shuffle in the boardroom and the appointment of James McCarron as sporting director, much of the day-to-day responsibility still lays with ‘Top’ and Rudkin.

According to recent reports, no takeover means no upcoming money for the Foxes. The financial hole they have dug for themselves will only get deeper.

As of the most recently published accounts, Leicester City have averaged losses of £60m per year for the past three seasons. Past accounts demonstrated their debt sat at a monstrous £163m.

Now, LCFC are without the Premier League riches, and revenue on the whole will decrease drastically while they stay in League One. To find some sort of salvation without a takeover, the Foxes simply have to be successful on the pitch.

An extended stint in League One will only see them burn a deeper hole in their pockets, and it will be increasingly more difficult to clamber out of it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cardiff City haven't been the busiest side in the EFL in the transfer market over the past few seasons, so need their new signings to hit the ground immediately.
  • The Bluebirds only brought in four new faces to the Cardiff City Stadium this summer, and even then, of the four, only two of them were actual new players who hadn't made their debuts for the club yet.
  • One of them, Nathan Trott, had a loan move made permanent, and another, Callum Scanlon, was signed on loan again from Liverpool after spending the second half of last season in South Wales.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cardiff City haven't been the busiest side in the EFL in the transfer market over the past few seasons, so need their new signings to hit the ground immediately. Therefore, they'll be happy that Millwall beat them to the signing of Yanis Issoufou.

The Bluebirds only brought in four new faces to the Cardiff City Stadium this summer, and even then, of the four, only two of them were actual new players who hadn't made their debuts for the club yet.

One of them, Nathan Trott, had a loan move made permanent, and another, Callum Scanlon, was signed on loan again from Liverpool after spending the second half of last season in South Wales.

That summer window followed the one last season where only Trott, Gabriel Osho and Omari Kellyman were signed in Brian Barry-Murphy's first window at the club. An admirable tactic to focus on promoting youth, but it puts the onus on those few who do sign to make an instant impact.

One player who Cardiff were linked with this past summer who didn't end up signing for them was 19-year-old Yanis Issoufou, who had broken through at Montpellier after their relegation to the French second tier last season.

He spent the entire first half of the season with the club's second team, appearing as a substitute in the early rounds of the Coup De France, but in 2026, Zoumana Camara introduced him more into the first-team fold.

Issoufou started 11 league games in the second half of the campaign, scoring two and assisting two. His breakout performance came in the Coup De France Round of 32, where he scored and assisted in a 4-0 win over Ligue 1 side Metz.

He was raw but exciting, and has plenty of potential, the kind of player that Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy excels at getting the best out of. However, their reported pursuit was in vain, as Issoufou ended up moving to Millwall.

Millwall, a side that has excelled in recent times at plucking young, promising European talents and cultivating them into top Championship stars, secured the services of Issoufou for €2.5 million, equal to £2.1m.

Industry observers note that the former French Under-19 international spent his entire career so far in his native country, coming through at Nimes Olympique before moving to Montpellier. This is his first venture into English football, and he hasn't yet settled in.

In a recent development, issoufou has played just 105 Championship minutes so far for Millwall, with all five of his appearances coming off the bench. He's failed to make a matchday squad in four of the last five league games.

In a recent development, there is good reason for that, though. Millwall boss Alex Neil spoke in late October about how the 20-year-old came over to England as a teenager with limited English and how he's still getting used to football and life in another country.

In the meantime, Issoufou is getting reps in with the club's Under-21s side, while helping him communicate better off the field and get up to speed with the intensity of Championship football.

Vincent Tan hasn't been the most benevolent owner in recent years at Cardiff, and the Bluebirds haven't ranked atop the player sales charts recently either, barring Mark McGuinness' move to Luton Town in the summer of 2024.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy did express some disappointment post-window at not being able to sign a winger or a striker on deadline day, stating that there were players they wanted to bring in, but it wasn't possible.

Ultimately, with marquee summer arrival Jack Moylan only arriving from Lincoln City for an initial £3 million, there's potential that the Bluebirds simply couldn't afford to spend £2.1 million on a winger who may not be ready to play regularly until January, or perhaps even next season.

Millwall, as a club, are in a position where they can afford to take time with some of their new signings, given the personnel that they have alongside Issoufou in the squad.

According to recent reports, do you think Yanis Issoufou will come good for Millwall? Let us know in the comments.

While the Frenchman gets up to speed, Alex Neil has the likes of Camiel Neghli, Kyrell Lisbie and Romain Esse to call upon in wide areas, so his absence isn't felt. At Cardiff, they need to be sure that who they're signing can be thrown straight into the side.

Right now, it looks like Cardiff are better off for not spending a seven-figure fee on Issoufou, but that doesn't mean they won't have any transfer envy in the years to come.

It's hard to really gauge the 20-year-old's ability right now, with just one shot, one chance created, and seven progressive carries in 105 minutes of football, but from his time at Montpellier, it's clear there's a player in there.

Millwall will have to be patient, but this is reflective of their current transfer strategy, one which is starting to reap rewards both in the transfer market, in future sales and in performances, with the Lions now highly regarded as on the cusp of promotion.

Perhaps in a year or so, Issoufou can help Alex Neil's side towards that, but for now, Cardiff aren't losing any sleep over losing out on the 20-year-old's services.

Lisandro Martinez could return to Manchester United’s starting line-up against Leeds United this weekend, with the defender reportedly available for selection after the controversy surrounding his comments about the club’s summer transfer business.

In a recent development, TEAMtalk transfer insider Graeme Bailey has suggested Michael Carrick could bring the Argentine straight back into the team for the trip to Elland Road. The fixture is expected to be a hostile occasion, making Martinez’s potential involvement an interesting one.

“I am told that Martinez is available for selection this weekend, and there is every chance Michael Carrick starts him,” Bailey said.

In a recent development, the defender recently found himself in trouble after questioning whether Manchester United had done enough in the summer transfer window. He apologised to the club’s hierarchy and was fined, but the incident has not apparently created a divide between him and the manager.

Bailey also dismissed suggestions that Martinez’s comments were an attack on Michael Carrick, insisting the defender and his teammates continue to support the head coach.

“Martinez was not critical of Carrick – far from it. This isn’t a repeat of something like Mo Salah criticising Arne Slot last season. It is almost the opposite.”.

According to Bailey, the United dressing room remains firmly behind Carrick despite the team’s disappointing start to the campaign. Senior players reportedly believe the current manager is still the right person to lead the team, rather than bringing in another face to replace him.

“Martinez and the squad are 100% behind Carrick. They know there is pressure after a poor start to the season, but they do not want to see a change.”.

Bailey went on to suggest that the fallout may have strengthened the bond between the players and their manager.

“Martinez and the senior players firmly believe nobody can come in and do a better job than Carrick. If anything, this has brought the group closer together.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:03 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 16:48 EST, 14 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

It has been revealed that 'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente noted. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols.

According to recent reports, 'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel remarked, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'.

Tuchel had earlier mentioned: 'It's important that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'.

England midfielder Declan Rice noted that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that James Trafford will face world champions Spain on Sunday night, raising questions over Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s No 1.

It was assumed that Pickford, who the head coach maintains is his first choice, would keep the jersey given the identity of the opposition and the chance for England to top their Nations League group with victory here in Madrid.

However, Tuchel will hand Leeds stopper Trafford his fifth cap at the Metropolitano Stadium.

It has been revealed that ’We want to try and see how far Traff is,’ remarked Tuchel, who rotated his keepers during last month’s international break. ‘So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match (2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday), so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers.

Industry observers note that ‘Tomorrow is a high-pressure match, on the biggest stage, and it's exactly what we need to see where we are with him (Trafford). Hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club.

'To have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up, and to show that you're ready.’.

It was put to Tuchel that it would make more sense to play the goalkeeper he believes is his No 1 in the biggest game from this round of fixtures.

According to recent reports, ’It was the circumstances of the last match, that we had some changes in the back four, and that was the decision in the goalkeeping team,’ he said. 'Jordan is at the moment our No.1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup.’.

Meanwhile, centre back Ezri Konsa is also set to start after recovering from a knee issue.

Industry observers note that ‘I’m very pleased with how he has fitted in seamlessly at Arsenal,’ mentioned Tuchel. ‘It just looks like he's always been there. For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.’.

PROBABLE ENGLAND XI: Trafford; White, Quansah, Konsa, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wolves duo Jordan James and Sean Neave were seen singing anti-West Brom chants at the Grand Slam of Darts in the city.
  • It has been an exciting start to the Championship season, with the Black Country rivals in the same league for the first time in five years.
  • And, they’ve both had a positive start to the season, with Cesar Peixoto’s side fourth in the table, and they’re only ahead of Albion on goals scored.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves duo Jordan James and Sean Neave were seen singing anti-West Brom chants at the Grand Slam of Darts in the city.

It has been an exciting start to the Championship season, with the Black Country rivals in the same league for the first time in five years.

And, they’ve both had a positive start to the season, with Cesar Peixoto’s side fourth in the table, and they’re only ahead of Albion on goals scored.

So, whilst there has always been a bitter rivalry between the two clubs, it is heightened this year, and Wanderers have the early bragging rights, having overcome Albion at Molineux by a single Fer Lopez goal back in September.

Such is the animosity between the two clubs, both sets of supporters can be heard singing about the other club at games every weekend.

However, it seems that it has now extended to the Grand Slam of Darts, which is being held in Wolverhampton this week.

That’s because, in a TikTok post uploaded by jackydangerbeard, shared on X by Talking Wolves, those inside the venue can be heard singing ‘**** the Albion’, with the footage showing that Neave and James are joining in.

As outlined above, this year has the potential to really ignite the rivalry between the two clubs, as it’s looking like both will be in the mix for promotion.

For Wolves, that won’t come as a surprise, as they were expected to be competing for automatic promotion following their relegation from the Premier League.

Albion are defying the pre-season predictions right now by pushing for a top two place though, but James Morrison will have full belief that his side can last the distance.

Having the two sides battling for promotion is nothing latest at this level, and it’s the Baggies that have had the upper hand over the years.

They overcame a ten-point gap in the final months of the 2001/02 campaign to finish in the top two, whilst they also beat Wolves over two legs in the 2006/07 play-offs, although they did then lose the final.

So, Wolves will feel they owe their rivals one this season, and it could add another dynamic to the rivalry if the two clubs are near the top of the table later in the season.

Will Wolves finish higher than West Brom this season? Let us know in the comments below.

It’s good to see the players enjoying themselves on a night out, and most Albion fans will recognise that it’s part of the banter that exists between the two clubs.

James is right now on loan at Wolves from Rennes, with the club having an option to buy, and Neave signed from Newcastle for this season.

Despite the pair not being permanent signings, they have clearly bought into what the Wolves, West Brom rivalry is all about, and it’s no surprise that fans of the Old Gold enjoyed their players getting involved with the chant.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen has been under fire recently, with poor performances prompting calls for Alphonse Areola to be brought into the starting XI. However, the Frenchman suffered an injury in the warm-up before WHUFC’s defeat to Blackburn Rovers before the break, ruling him out.

Industry observers note that and, after the international break, doubts remain over Areola’s availability. Speaking to the official club media ahead of Saturday’s clash with Preston North End, Scott Parker noted: “We’re struggling a bit with Alphonse at the moment. He probably looks a bit unlikely. We’ll probably leave it as late as we can to see if he’s fit to be involved.”.

Recent findings suggest that elsewhere, Max Kilman is suspended, but Kyle Walker-Peters could be in line for a return. Parker made no mention of the full-back in his pre-match interview, saying: “There’s nothing really jumping out, other than Alphonse.”.

Recent findings suggest that areola isn’t ruled out of West Ham’s clash with Preston North End, but it would be a surprise to see him start. If Parker goes into the weekend planning to start the Frenchman and it transpires that he isn’t ready to go on matchday, it throws that section of the pre-match preparations out of the window.

Despite his struggle for form, it is smarter to prepare for the game with Hermansen in goal. That will frustrate some sections of the WHUFC support, but it is the sensible move to make.

Hermansen has started every Championship game this season, but his performances have been far from convincing.

He isn’t solely responsible for the underwhelming defensive record of four clean sheets and 24 goals conceded in 16 games across all competitions. However, the Dane’s displays have left a lot to be desired with an inability to command his box and errors when coming to claim crosses leading to chances for the opposition.

In a recent development, given his form, a fully fit Areola may have got the nod. For this weekend though, it seems Hermansen will keep his place.

When Areola is at 100%, Hermansen will have a fight on his hands to keep his place.

Sources indicate that it means that if he does start again against Preston North End as expected, he needs to put in a far more assured performance. A clean sheet would not go amiss, but the most important thing is to act with confidence and conviction. If he can command his box, comfortably claim crosses and show composure on the ball, it will go a long way to easing concerns around his form.

If not, Areola will be waiting in the wings to come into the WHUFC side when fit. If his absence extends longer, then youngster Finlay Herrick may be considered if Parker feels a chance is needed.

Industry News: Kenny McLean teases Teemu Pukki return at Norwich City

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (760 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Norwich City captain Kenny McLean has "no doubt" that Teemu Pukki will be back at Carrow Road soon enough, after the ex-Canaries frontman hung up his boots earlier this month.
  • Pukki is highly regarded as a modern-day Norwich legend, netting 88 times in 210 appearances for the Canaries over five years at the club, which included 29-goal and 26-goal campaigns in their Championship title-winning terms under Daniel Farke in 2018/19 and 2020/21.
  • The all-time top scorer for the Finnish national team left Norwich back in 2023, and after a year and a half in the MLS with Minnesota, re-joined HJK Helsinki to see out the rest of his career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Norwich City captain Kenny McLean has "no doubt" that Teemu Pukki will be back at Carrow Road soon enough, after the ex-Canaries frontman hung up his boots earlier this month.

Pukki is highly regarded as a modern-day Norwich legend, netting 88 times in 210 appearances for the Canaries over five years at the club, which included 29-goal and 26-goal campaigns in their Championship title-winning terms under Daniel Farke in 2018/19 and 2020/21.

The all-time top scorer for the Finnish national team left Norwich back in 2023, and after a year and a half in the MLS with Minnesota, re-joined HJK Helsinki to see out the rest of his career.

He bowed out with 11 goals and 13 assists in 42 games in all competitions in the Finnish capital, but couldn't end with a title, after a 3-3 draw on the final day of the season against AC Oulu handed the trophy to Inter Turku.

Despite not ending with silverware, Pukki bows out as a legend for numerous different clubs, but none more so than at Norwich.

He created plenty of memories at Carrow Road, and current Canaries captain Kenny McLean, who joined Norwich at the same time as Pukki did back in the summer of 2018 and is now in his ninth season in Norfolk, shared them with him.

Evidently, there's a mutual respect and friendship between the two, and the 34-year-old hailed an incredible career after the Finnish marksman's retirement was confirmed.

Sources indicate that "An incredible career, and the status that he has at this football club is undeniable. He's undoubtedly a legend, and I think everybody would back me up in saying that," McLean said, per the Pink Un.

It has been revealed that "I spoke to him last week after his final game. I think it's definitely time for him – that's where he seems to be. He's got three young children and his wife, Kiki, so they can go and spend some time together.

"He deserves it because he's had a hell of a career, some ups and some downs, and thankfully some success along the way here.".

With Pukki finding his Saturdays free now, though, there's one question on Norwich fans' minds: when are we going to see him back at Carrow Road?

"He'll be over at some point, no doubt, but I think I'll let him have some time with the family first," McLean responded.

Those Daniel Farke-led Norwich squads, especially in the Championship, were a joy to watch, and Canaries fans loved them.

Evidently, the camaraderie amongst the group was high, too, and it needed to be, with the majority of them enduring the highest highs of second-tier title wins, but also the lowest lows during the subsequent relegation campaigns out of the Premier League.

Pukki even said in an interview back in June that he'd created quite a close bond with McLean and his compatriot Grant Hanley during his time at Norwich, with those two part of both title-winning teams.

Is Teemu Pukki the best modern-day Norwich City striker? Let us know what you think in the comments.

It's not often that a well-liked squad can spend a few years together at one club, and those in the stands at Carrow Road still reminisce about those years, with those teams being the last ones to oversee success in the Championship.

Therefore, they'll be delighted to see them all remaining close long after they'd gone their separate ways.

But despite the good feeling that surrounds the entire squad from that era at Norwich, there's no one more well-liked amongst the Canaries fanbase than Pukki.

The Finnish frontman immediately endeared himself to the Norwich fanbase with a Golden Boot-winning campaign in his first season in England, and then followed that up with 11 goals in the Premier League, including a hat-trick against Newcastle United and strikes against Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City.

Given his excellence in the division below and the ability he showed in the top flight, there'd have been few who would have held it against Pukki for wanting to continue his career in the Premier League or elsewhere after relegation in 2020, but the striker stayed.

What followed was another emphatic scoring season and another 11-goal campaign in the top flight, with his loyalty to the club celebrated alongside all the goals he was scoring.

Norwich fans will be making sure they're inside Carrow Road when the Finnish legend makes his return to Norfolk, and they'll be ready to give him the praise he clearly deserves.

  • Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right.
  • The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, manchester United had a difficult evening once again as they were held to a 1-1 draw at Leeds United. Pressure mounts on Michael Carrick as United have just 7 points from 7 games.

Manchester United took the lead through Bryan Mbeumo in the first half, with the forward finishing Youri Tielemans’ excellent cross from the right. However, the visitors couldn’t hold on to their advantage as Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds United from a corner.

The draw extended United’s frustrating run of results, leaving Michael Carrick still searching for the consistency his side need.

Carragher, though, believes there were positives to take from the trip, particularly one performance at the back.

Jamie Carragher has singled out Harry Maguire for praise after Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United at Elland Road on Sunday.

Speaking on Sky Sports, the former Liverpool defender admitted that picking up a point at Elland Road was not necessarily a bad result in isolation, even if United’s recent form made it feel like a missed opportunity.

“Going away to Leeds is going to be tricky for any team except for Manchester City and Arsenal at the moment,” Carragher stated.

“A lot of teams will take a point at Leeds this season but the problem for Manchester United is the results have been so poor that they need to start winning games so it almost feels like two points dropped.”.

Carragher then turned his attention to Maguire, who he felt played a major role in keeping United in the game when Leeds began to push for a winner.

In a recent development, “But in isolation, getting a point at Leeds is a decent result. I thought Harry Maguire was fantastic, especially in the second half.”.

According to recent reports, leeds United grew into the contest after Calvert-Lewin brought them level, putting United under pressure during the closing stages. Carragher felt Maguire’s efforts in defence helped prevent the visitors from falling apart.

“After Leeds got that goal back there was a stage of the game where it felt like Man United could go under, but Maguire at the back held it together for them. He was fantastic.”.

The result may feel like another opportunity missed for Carrick, but Maguire’s performance gave United something positive to take away from Elland Road.

Como vs Man Utd Preview: Team news, injuries, form and where to watch

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.
  • Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season.
  • The pressure on Carrick continues to grow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

Industry observers note that united have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Sources indicate that lisandro Martinez is a major concern after coming off at half-time against Leeds with a thigh problem. Ayden Heaven, Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo are all doubtful for the game.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular concern.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

#37891. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
