England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6458 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

The world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Sources indicate that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

According to recent reports, that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

Sources indicate that on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

Industry observers note that it could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Recent findings suggest that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

According to recent reports, afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

The irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another big chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

According to recent reports, the manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

Industry observers note that it was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Recent findings suggest that spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Recent findings suggest that now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Sources indicate that then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

Industry observers note that it could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

Industry observers note that ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was quickly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Recent findings suggest that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

It has been revealed that “I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

“It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We revealed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

Sources indicate that “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

Recent findings suggest that marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon claims mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

Recent findings suggest that A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

Industry observers note that england have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

It has been revealed that baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

It has been revealed that garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

According to recent reports, double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

Saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

Sources indicate that the way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that “This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

It has been revealed that “There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

It has been revealed that england begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

Industry observers note that england’s prepares for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel remarked. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

“For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

According to recent reports, declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Industry observers note that trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against Upcoming Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Industry observers note that having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough may be flying high in the Championship at present, but they are reportedly at risk of losing star midfielder, Aidan Morris.

According to German publication, BILD, the American is one of three second tier stars at the moment being eyed by Bundesliga outfit, VfB Stuttgart, with the January transfer window edging ever closer.

Kim Hellberg has restructured his squad at the Riverside Stadium for the current campaign, 12 months on from his initial appointment in place of controversial former head coach, Rob Edwards.

Boro enjoyed a remarkable recruitment drive by adding the likes of Radek Vitek, Ash Phillips, Max Arfsten, Sebastian Berhalter, Amario Cozier-Duberry and Will Lankshear to the Swede's ranks, despite the high-profile sale of Hayden Hackney to Everton following May's play-off final defeat.

Morris has since upped his performance levels even further in the first 15 games of the Championship season, with the North East side sat second as a three-goal swing is all separating them and current leaders, Birmingham City.

Morris, 25, arrived on Teesside from Major League Soccer outfit, Columbus Crew, two summers ago in a $4m (£3m) deal, and has since become one of Middlesbrough's key men.

The 14-time USMNT international is nearing 100 Championship appearances, having only missed the opening-day victory over Lincoln City so far this season whilst also netting against Burnley and Bolton Wanderers, with the strike at Turf Moore being his first for the club.

Morris' all-round play has been integral to the way in which Hellberg's side create a bundle of chances in the majority of fixtures, and it was claimed last month that clubs on the continent had been alerted by such performances, although Tom Bogert's report also revealed his desire to lead Middlesbrough back to the Premier League.

However, BILD's fresh report claims Morris is being identified as a potential replacement for Angelo Stiller, whose future at the Mercedes-Benz Arena is far from certain, with AC Milan credited with interest in the nine-cap German international.

Stiller's contract expires in 2028, and there are suggestions that he may be sold next summer in a bid for Stuttgart to make a strong sum of cash from his services.

It comes as no real surprise that Morris' collection of strong performances at the Riverside have attracted potential suitors, but such exit talk involving the American also revolves around the futures of two divisional counterparts.

Stuttgart were heavily linked with a move for Southampton's Caspar Jander earlier in the year. It was claimed after the Spygate scandal that the 23-year-old was seeking an exit from St Mary's after the German top-flight club's initial interest surfaced.

Jander remained on the South Coast but has endured an injury-hit start to the season, and BILD report that there are still question marks from the UEFA Champions League-competing outfit over a €25m price-tag.

It has also emerged that Sebastian Hoeneß's side have earmarked Arne Engels as a potential target, three months on from the Belgian's £22m switch from Celtic to West Ham United which smashed the EFL's all-time transfer record.

The Belgian has made 14 Championship appearances for the Hammers so far, scoring once and providing three assists.

Morris' influence under Hellberg is echoed by the fact he has averaged the second-highest number of accurate passes per 90 in the Championship, ironically behind Middlesbrough defender, Adilson Malanda.

Luke Graham seizes his chance to shine in Scotland back-line... now Stoke defender aims to make himself a fixture for years to come

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In a recent development, in five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

Sources indicate that this does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win.

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he stated.

‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

It has been revealed that ‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’.

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was announced as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream rapidly become reality.

‘I’ve always noted that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off.

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

Industry observers note that ‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

‘He just remarked to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’.

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’.

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden.

With the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

In a recent development, ‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ stated Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’.

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham mentioned. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of fresh, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’.

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season.

It has been revealed that graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

Industry observers note that ‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

Industry observers note that ‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. His performance reminded Rio Ferdinand why he had been talking about the youngster throughout the previous year and during the summer transfer window.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand highlighted how Bouaddi was the highlight of the game against PSG and who they missed.

“He came on and demonstrated PSG that they may have missed out on someone who was on their doorstep when he was playing in France,” Ferdinand mentioned.

The former England international also confirmed that Manchester United had been interested in bringing the midfielder to Old Trafford, but the transfer fee was too expensive.

“Manchester United were in for him, 100%, but the fee was just too much,” he added.

Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”.

Rio Ferdinand suggested Bouaddi’s quality could soon make the midfield position in a packed Manchester City his regular role.

City already have Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez among their midfield options, but Ferdinand believes Bouaddi has the ability to stand out alongside them.

“They’ve got Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez in that midfield as well but this kid could be the best of the three, easily.”.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Industry observers note that carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville remarked in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he noted.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liam Bridcutt has become the latest one-time Championship player to land a job on the managerial circuit, with his appointment at Ashington AFC confirmed on Wednesday evening.
  • The 37-year-old was a regular fixture in English football's second tier throughout the 2010s, having initially helped Brighton and Hove Albion return to the division after a six-year absence under Gus Poyet for the 2011/12 campaign.
  • Bridcutt also made several appearances in League One for various clubs, as well as achieving gametime in the Premier League during a mixed spell with Sunderland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liam Bridcutt has become the latest one-time Championship player to land a job on the managerial circuit, with his appointment at Ashington AFC confirmed on Wednesday evening.

The 37-year-old was a regular fixture in English football's second tier throughout the 2010s, having initially helped Brighton and Hove Albion return to the division after a six-year absence under Gus Poyet for the 2011/12 campaign.

Bridcutt also made several appearances in League One for various clubs, as well as achieving gametime in the Premier League during a mixed spell with Sunderland.

There have been many surprise moves into the non-league game from former Championship stars in recent months.

Kyle Hudlin and Britt Assombalonga are now a strike partnership at National League South outfit, Harborough Town, all of Chey Dunkley, Ryan Woods, Marvin Johnson and Elias Kachunga linking up at Solihull Moors of the National League, whilst former Burnley and Derby County star, Jeff Hendrick has confirmed his role as ambassador at Ebbsfleet United.

Bridcutt ended his playing career two years ago, and since then has obtained coaching roles, but will now lead a side in the dugout for the very first time.

After confirming his retirement from playing in February 2024, the two-time Scotland international landed his first coaching role seven months' later by becoming a sessional coach within Newcastle United's academy setup despite his prior connections with the Magpies' bitter North East rivals.

Soon afterwards, though, Bridcutt joined another local side in the form of Gateshead, becoming assistant to Carl Magnay in October 2024, although the boss of the National League club would resign at the end of 2024/25 after missing out on a play-off spot by one point.

Just two weeks ago, the former midfielder became part of Ashington's interim management setup with Paul Dunn, having previously been an associate of head of football, Ian Skinner, during his spell at Gateshead.

The Northern Premier League Division One East side then confirmed that Bridcutt had accepted the offer of becoming permanent manager at Woodhorn Lane in midweek, with it being claimed: "The appointment represents an exciting step for Ashington AFC as the club looks ahead to the next chapter of its footballing journey.".

Ashington are presently 20th in the table, inside the relegation zone, having accumulated 16 points from their opening 18 fixtures.

Many who supported clubs in the Championship within recent times are likely to have been intrigued by Ashington's managerial appointment, as Bridcutt was often credited for being underrated in his defensive midfield role for various clubs in the division.

He made 182 of his 383 career appearances in the second tier, which included guiding Brighton to the 2012/13 play-off semi-finals, where they were defeated by M23 rivals, Crystal Palace.

How underrated was Liam Bridcutt in the Championship? Comment below!

After signing for Sunderland in a £2.5m deal, Bridcutt made just 30 Premier League appearances and later returned to the Championship to turn out for the likes of Leeds, where he was appointed captain in 2016 under Garry Monk, as well as Nottingham Forest and and Blackpool.

As well as earning promotion from League One with Brighton, Bridcutt also made appearances in the third tier for Lincoln City and Bolton Wanderers, with the Imps defeated against his future employers, Blackpool, in the 2021 play-off final at Wembley.

Bridcutt is yet to speak to the media following his appointment with Ashington, but given his vast experience within the EFL and Premier League as a player and coach, he will be hoping to continue the area's proud footballing legacy.

Indeed, two of the country's most famous footballers, Sir Bobby Charlton and Jack Charlton, hailed from the Northumberland village before being a part of England's only FIFA World Cup-winning squad in 1966.

It remains to be seen what the future holds for Bridcutt on the managerial circuit, but he will hope it starts with a crucial victory against Morpeth Town on Friday.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

Recent findings suggest that those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Sources indicate that carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”.

If United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no intends to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

Sources indicate that for now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

According to recent reports, that’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

Sources indicate that ‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ said the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

It has been revealed that ‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden.

Sources indicate that ‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

It has been revealed that ‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is notable he knows that.’.

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – currently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show.

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ remarked Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

In a recent development, ‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

‘It is part of the process to play away against a top team. That is not something we have done yet. The approach will be different and, for me as a coach, it is a game with a lot of responsibility.’.

Swansea City are on the hunt for a new head coach after Vitor Matos departed for Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, and both Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick are among the contenders to replace him.

The Championship side has yet to formally announce Matos' departure, but the BlueCo-led French outfit confirmed his arrival on Wednesday, with the Swans set to receive around £5 million in compensation for his services.

Matos leaves Swansea having taken them from 20th in the second tier upon his arrival midway through last season all the way to the summit in the early stages of the ongoing campaign.

A run of four defeats in five leading up to the November international break saw them drop to sixth, but they're still three points off Birmingham City, who currently occupy the top spot.

Now, Swansea have to source someone who can maintain their strong start, as they look to mount a promotion challenge after five consecutive campaigns finishing between 10th and 15th.

According to TalkSPORT's Alex Crook, two of the early candidates to replace Vitor Matos as Swansea boss are former Wolves head coach Rob Edwards and Liverpool coach Tommy Elphick.

Edwards has been out of work since the summer, when he was rather unceremoniously sacked by Wolves following their relegation from the Premier League. He found out the news from social media while he was on holiday, after being one of the driving forces behind the signing of Kieran Trippier and the return of Raul Jimenez.

It has been revealed that in the Championship, he has experience at the top end of the table. He took Luton Town up into the Premier League in the 2022/23 campaign, and last season had Middlesbrough battling amongst the automatic promotion places before leaving for Molineux.

He has had his failings at this level, though, such as with Luton following their relegation from the top flight and at Watford for a brief period in 2022, although he isn't the only manager to fall victim to the events at Vicarage Road.

Meanwhile, this isn't the first time that Elphick has been linked with a head coach role at Championship level. The former Bournemouth defender rejected the opportunity to take over at Bristol City during their managerial search during the off-season, instead following Andoni Iraola to form part of his coaching staff at Liverpool.

The 39-year-old has coached ever since his retirement in 2021, being part of the first-team staff at the Vitality Stadium since Gary O'Neil's time at the club in 2022, until he left for Anfield in the summer.

It has been revealed that swansea fans are still stung by Matos' departure and the haste with which it happened. Strasbourg's official approach only took place on Monday, with this whole ordeal coming quite out of the blue.

Those at the Swansea.com Stadium had become admirers of the football being played under the Portuguese boss, playing high-intensity, pressing football while also being good in possession, too. Replacing him will be difficult, and supporters online aren't enamoured by the reports linking their post with Edwards and Elphick.

The majority of the discourse is coming Edwards' way, though.

The 43-year-old isn't seen as an inspiring choice, even despite his relative success at Championship level, and some Swans fans don't think he'd be able to oversee a smooth transition from the football seen under Matos.

"Don’t particularly want us to go down the Rob Edwards route to be honest, as I’m not convinced he’s the right fit for us in terms of style of play," one fan mentioned in response to the reports.

"If it is Rob Edwards I'd be extremely disappointed. Would undo all the good work we've done over the last year," another remarked, while a third commented, "It’s just so underwhelming, isn’t it?".

Even one fan commented, "Rob Edwards, no, Tommy Elphick, yes," indicating that they'd rather have someone who hasn't been a head coach yet in his career over Edwards at this stage of the season.

Swansea went against the grain and took a risk with hiring Matos back in November last year. The then-37-year-old was incredibly inexperienced as a main dugout man, taking charge of 12 games for Portuguese side Maritimo before heading to South Wales.

Especially with the club being advised by Jamestown Analytics now, the data company founded by Brighton and Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom, perhaps it should be expected that Matos' replacement will equally be out of left-field, if the data can advise manager hires, that is.

Elphick seems destined to become a head coach someday, with him learning under one of the best up-and-coming bosses in the English game right now, in Iraola, and his time at Liverpool will expose him to coaching better players against elite opposition both domestically and in Europe.

Who do you think Swansea City will hire to replace Vitor Matos? Let us know in the comments.

It's also worth noting that there's an easy comparison between Matos and Elphick, not just in their relative managerial inexperience, but also in the fact that they've spent time at Anfield in the dugout, with the now-Strasbourg head coach learning under Jürgen Klopp for nearly five years.

It will be interesting to see where Swansea go from Matos; whether they'll hire someone more well-known who could maintain play-off form, or if they bring in someone to help grow with them, like they did this time last year.

United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.

The club stated it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.

Neville had already branded the process “classless” on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, pointing out that it was widely known Carrick was about to go while United were holding talks with potential replacements.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the decision was confirmed, the former United captain went even further.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” he said.

“That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”.

Neville took particular aim at the decision to hold the crucial meeting in Monaco, with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flying out to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that it seems the only ones not to realise that are the trio above, but they aren’t stupid. How they explain it, or attempt to rationalise, it will be painful to listen to.

Neville also argued the club should have acted sooner. Looking back to the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in October, he said United “effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch” as he waved goodbye to supporters at full time, only for the board to hand him three more games.

He summed up the episode as “indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership”.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years.
  • In a recent development, reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision.
  • The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chelsea fans have followed Manchester City’s financial rules case for years. Everyone at Stamford Bridge knows a guilty verdict could cost City serious money, and much of it could end up with rivals lower down the table.

In a recent development, reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

According to recent reports, this matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

Sources indicate that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

Manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

Sources indicate that that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

Data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

Within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

Prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

For Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a big boost. It could help fund fresh signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

It has been revealed that city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

Chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

According to recent reports, the Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Mauricio Pochettino officially begins work as United head coach on Wednesday, just four days before his first match against Liverpool at Anfield.

The 54-year-old replaces Michael Carrick, who was dismissed last week after United won just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them 18th in the table.

Pochettino arrives after completing his final assignment with the United States, who beat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

The Argentine has signed a contract until the summer of 2029 and is expected to meet his newly introduced players and oversee his first training session on Thursday.

Speaking after his final match with the United States, Pochettino acknowledged the challenge awaiting him in Manchester.

“The fresh challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he said.

Sources indicate that several members of his coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez, travelled to Manchester earlier this week to begin preparations. Pochettino will have limited time to work with his squad before Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool, which kicks off at 4.30pm GMT.

The former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager inherits a United side struggling for results after a difficult opening to the campaign. He previously guided Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final and won the French league title during his spell with Paris Saint-Germain.

United’s next fixtures also include a Champions League trip to Sporting CP and a home Premier League match against Brentford. Pochettino’s immediate task is to improve United’s league position, beginning with a demanding first match at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that gittens picked up the knock after a challenge during the second half of England’s win over Kazakhstan. He was withdrawn as a precaution. “Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

Given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Former Manchester United midfielder Juan Mata has declared his retirement from professional football at the age of 38, bringing an end to a beautiful career of around 20 years.

The Spaniard went on to win one of the biggest trophies in professional football. The former Manchester United midfielder confirmed his decision on Wednesday after ending his playing career with Australian side Melbourne Victory.

Mata enjoyed a memorable spell at Manchester United after arriving from Chelsea in January 2014. He spent more than eight years at Old Trafford, making 285 appearances, scoring 51 goals and winning four trophies.

Sources indicate that his first trophy with Manchester United came in the 2016 FA Cup final against Crystal Palace. He also helped the club win the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League during the 2016/17 campaign.

In a recent development, before moving to Manchester, Juan Mata had established himself as one of Chelsea’s most creative players. He won the club’s Player of the Year award in both of his first two full seasons at Stamford Bridge before eventually joining United as David Moyes’ marquee signing.

Mata probably had the biggest moments of his career in the Spain shirt. He earned 41 international caps and scored 10 goals, becoming part of the most talented Spanish team in history. He went on to win the 2010 FIFA World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain while etching his name in Spanish football history with a goal in Spain’s 4-0 victory over Italy in the European Championship final.

After leaving Manchester United in 2022, the midfielder continued his career with Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe and Western Sydney Wanderers before joining Melbourne Victory in September 2025.

His final season in Australia was an impressive one. Mata registered five goals and 13 assists, won the Johnny Warren Medal and earned a place in the A-League Team of the Season.

“Football will never leave my life. There are so many ways to continue loving the game.”.

Sources indicate that nothing in D’Amico’s comments suggests Roma are open to a sale in the near term, and Koné has given no sign that he wants to leave. The £86m valuation, reported by Football London, stands as Roma’s marker rather than an asking price involved with Chelsea.

Will Chelsea return with a more formal approach in a future window? D’Amico’s comments give no hint either way. The Manu Koné Chelsea transfer link is unlikely to fade given Chelsea’s history of scouting France’s leading midfielders, but any fresh move will have to wait for Roma’s stance to soften.

Amid the clamour for a change at the helm following another poor showing at a major tournament, it was easy to lose sight of the reality of the situation.

Sources indicate that steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. According to recent reports, sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden.

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

According to recent reports, ‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ remarked the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most important thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

Sources indicate that ‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create big chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’.

Recent findings suggest that if that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

Sources indicate that ‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia.

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

Industry observers note that ‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’.

Give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

The sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

Sources indicate that ‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’.

Even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli.

Sources indicate that ‘We need to play slightly better,’ he said. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’.

Friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

The brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

In a recent development, ‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

‘So, we had a wee chat and I think we both remarked the most important thing was just no matter who hit it, hit the back of the net.’.

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high.

Industry observers note that tomorrow, the equation is clear. To finish second in the Nations League group and secure a place in pot two for the Euro draw, Scotland must beat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t beat North Macedonia.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

Sources indicate that ‘Difficult,’ mentioned McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

According to recent reports, ‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’.

Manchester United are prepared to consider legal action if evidence emerges that another club approached academy forward JJ Gabriel without permission.

In a recent development, the 16-year-old announced his departure from Old Trafford in a social media video on Tuesday and is expected to join Real Madrid in January. According to The Times and ESPN, United remain concerned about the circumstances surrounding his proposed move, although no breach of transfer regulations has been established.

According to recent reports, gabriel has been absent from United since September, when he requested the cancellation of his registration. The teenager remains registered with the club, and United could explore legal or regulatory options if evidence of an unauthorised approach emerges.

The Independent reports that United do not want to punish Gabriel for actions they believe may have been taken by adults involved in his future. Real Madrid have been widely linked with the forward, but his transfer has not been formally completed.

Gabriel joined United’s academy in 2020 and was named the club’s young player of the year last season. He featured for the senior side during pre-season but has not made a competitive first-team appearance.

According to recent reports, the youngster is eligible for a move within the European Union under an exception to FIFA’s rules on international transfers involving players aged under 18. In his farewell message, Gabriel thanked United for helping him develop during his six years at the club.

According to recent reports, his expected move to Madrid would bring that association to an end, although questions remain over the process leading to his departure. United have not declared legal proceedings, and there has been no finding of wrongdoing by Real Madrid or any other club.

Leeds United have reportedly suffered a major blow in their January pursuit of Stuttgart attacker Bilal El Khannous.

Unlike last campaign, Leeds appear in no real danger of a relegation dogfight this term, with the Elland Road club losing just two of their opening 10 league games as they sit ninth in the Premier League table.

The Whites recorded their third victory of the top-flight schedule with a 1-0 success over Tottenham Hotspur in Yorkshire prior to the international break, with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge next up on Saturday afternoon.

Looking set to take Leeds to the status of an established Premier League outfit, head coach Farke is in line for a latest contract - a stark contrast to his days of struggles in the same division with Norwich City.

As per Football Insider, Leeds are long-term admirers of El Khannous, who was a bright spark for Leicester City as they were relegated from the Premier League during the 2024-25 campaign.

The Morocco international did not stick around at the King Power Stadium for a season in the Championship, instead securing an initial loan switch to Stuttgart in the Bundesliga in September 2025.

It is understood that Leeds were keen on bringing El Khannous to Elland Road during the upcoming January transfer window, however, that now appears extremely unlikely to occur.

Stuttgart are supposedly unwilling to sanction a mid-season departure for the former Leicester playmaker, who is a regular starter for Sebastian Hoeness in the Bundesliga this term.

Adding to the difficulty of a potential deal, El Khannous recently signed a long-term contract with the German club, meaning that it would take a significant fee to prize him away from MHP Arena.

During his first campaign at MHP Arena, El Khannous helped Stuttgart to a fourth-placed finish in the Bundesliga, securing Champions League football for the current season.

Whilst Leeds are certainly a mid-ranking Premier League football, they are not currently in the position to offer European football, so a move to Elland Road would be a step down in that way.

However, the pull of the English game is strong, and there is a chance that El Khannous returns to the Premier League at some point, potentially during 2027's summer window.

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Sources indicate that chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

Industry observers note that the most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater stated.

According to recent reports, one off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day intends back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Industry observers note that chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

In a recent development, drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

Sources indicate that that tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing major calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar glitch. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s aims after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

In this, the second week of the second international break of the season, there’s an understandable eagerness amongst fans to get back to the serious business of league football again this coming weekend.

However there is still a crucial fixture tonight, before the autumn internationals are concluded, in which West Ham supporters should take an interest.

Greece against Serbia in the UEFA Nations League Group A hardly sets the pulse racing as a neutral: It’s normally a game I could happily ignore but it takes on a special meaning after West Ham’s Dinos Mavropanos performed so poorly in the crushing 7 – 0 defeat by the Netherlands last time out.

Consequently I will be taking a bit of an interest in this somewhat obscure game to see how West Ham’s number 15 is looking after such a demoralising result three days ago,.

West Ham need Mavropanos to return having put the 7 – 0 thrashing firmly behind him.

West Ham’s main man took a bit of a pasting in the Greek media after the game, in what was described as the ‘blackest night‘ for Greek football.

West Ham, already without Maximilian Kilman, remember, banned for the upcoming Saturday tie against Preston North End, will be keeping everything crossed that their one remaining senior centre-back has a solid evening facing up to the likes of Mitrovic, Jovic and co.

Scott Parker already has a selection dilemma over bringing in teenager Airidas Golambeckis or loanee Morato to replace Kilman.

The last thing he or West Ham need is another shaky Mavropanos performance tonight and a return to the ‘Mavropanic’ days of the past – which another heavy defeat could usher back in.

West Ham return to championship football on Saturday with the visit of Preston North End and must do so without one of their ever-presents this season, Maximilian Kilman, who is suspended for the home game.

However, a strong response against Bournemouth would go a long way towards easing the pressure and restoring belief.
